results.rationale: A binary tree is a specific type of tree where each node has at most two children, so it is defined and built on the concept of a tree.

A binary search tree is a specific type of binary tree where each node's left child has a value less than the node and its right child has a value greater than the node, making it impossible to understand BSTs without first understanding the general concept of binary trees.
AVL Trees are a self-balancing implementation of Binary Search Trees, making it impossible to understand AVL Trees without first understanding the concept of Binary Search Trees.
Binary Trees are a specialisation of Recursion, as they are a type of recursive data structure, where each node has at most two children.
A graph is a more general concept than a tree, as it can be cyclic, whereas a tree is a specific type of graph with a root and no cycles.
AVL Trees are a type of self-balancing binary search tree, which is a specific implementation detail and does not inherently rely on the general concept of graphs.
